content.text:
**Recent major changes to the xAI Grok API (as of mid-2026) include significant model consolidations, new releases, pricing adjustments, and feature updates.**

### May 15, 2026: Major Model Retirement and Consolidation
xAI retired eight older model variants effective May 15, 2026, at 12:00 PM PT, redirecting traffic to a single primary model (`grok-4.3`) to streamline the API.[[1]](https://docs.x.ai/developers/migration/may-15-retirement)

Retired models included:
- `grok-4-1-fast-reasoning` / `grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning`
- `grok-4-fast-reasoning` / `grok-4-fast-non-reasoning`
- `grok-4-0709`
- `grok-code-fast-1`
- `grok-3`
- `grok-imagine-image-pro`

**Redirect behavior**:
- Most reasoning variants → `grok-4.3` (with low or none reasoning effort).
- `grok-code-fast-1` → `grok-build-0.1`.
- `grok-imagine-image-pro` → `grok-imagine-image-quality` (later further redirected; see below).

**Pricing impact**: Deprecated slugs are now billed at `grok-4.3` rates ($1.25/M input, $2.50/M output). The company warned that redirects may break streaming or function-calling in some cases.[[2]](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/xai-cuts-grok-api-to-single-model-at-125m)

This simplified the fragmented catalog into fewer flagship models.

### New Model Releases (2026)
- **Grok 4.6** (August 12, 2026): Frontier model optimized for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work. Features a 500k token context window, text + image input, configurable reasoning effort (low/medium/high/default/xhigh), and tools like function calling, web/X search, and code execution. Pricing: ~$2/M input and $6/M output (with caching discounts and long-context tiers). Available via API, Grok Build, Cursor, and gateways like OpenRouter.[[3]](https://x.ai/docs/developers/grok-4-5)

- **Grok 4.5** (July 2026): Similar focus on coding/agentic work; rolled out to EU users and added to the lineup. Pricing aligns with 4.6 in many tiers.[[4]](https://x.ai/docs/release-notes)

- **grok-build-0.1** (May 2026): Cost-effective model for agentic coding (same as Grok Build CLI). Priced at $1/M input and $2/M output.[[5]](https://x.com/xai/status/2060392252858589669)

Additional releases include image/video models like `grok-imagine-video-1.5` (with expanded modalities and 1080p support) and updates to speech/voice features.[[4]](https://x.ai/docs/release-notes)

### Upcoming Retirement (November 2, 2026)
`grok-imagine-image-quality` will be retired, with requests redirecting to `grok-imagine-image-2.0` (at low quality). This offers lower pricing in many cases and expanded capabilities (e.g., aspect ratios, more source images). A 60-day notice was issued on September 2, 2026.[[6]](https://docs.x.ai/developers/migration/imagine-image-quality-nov-2)

### Pricing and Advanced Features
Current text API pricing (per 1M tokens, with short/long context tiers and caching discounts) centers on models like `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.5`, `grok-4.3`, and `grok-build-0.1`. Imagine (image/video) and Voice APIs have separate per-image/second/character rates. Batch API offers discounts for asynchronous workloads (not supported on the newest models like 4.6).[[7]](https://x.ai/docs/developers/pricing)

**Other updates**:
- Enhanced Responses API with better tool calling (OpenAI-compatible + native server-side tools like web/X search and code interpreter).
- "Grok Skills" for persistent custom expertise across sessions.
- Console improvements, usage insights, mobile support, and Batch API for high-volume processing.[[8]](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/05/xai-grok-skills/)

- X (formerly Twitter) API updates in 2026 introduced usage-based pricing and xAI credit incentives tied to X spend.[[9]](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/x-formerly-twitter-announces-new-api-pricing-structure-xai/811667/)

For the latest details, check the official docs at [x.ai/docs](https://x.ai/docs) or the console at [console.x.ai](https://console.x.ai). The API remains compatible with OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs for easy migration. Older references to Grok 4.1 variants are now historical, as they were retired in the May consolidation.[[10]](https://www.therundown.ai/tools/grok-4-1)

These changes reflect xAI's focus on fewer, more capable models with better tooling for developers.
